transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm happy to help you with any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start with light gardening about 1 week after surgery. Just be gentle with yourself and avoid heavy lifting or bending. It's also a good idea to wear protective eyewear when gardening to avoid any water or debris getting in your eyes. Does that help? Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that helps a lot, thank you! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should start using your preservative-free eye drops four times daily to help with dryness. You can start using them right away, actually. Just make sure to get them from the pharmacist and follow the instructions. If you were using eye drops before your surgery, it's also safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information! I'm also wondering, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light after cataract surgery, especially in bright sunlight. If it's mild and just seems brighter than usual, you can try wearing sunglasses to help with it. But if the sensitivity is severe or accompanied by redness and pain, we may need to check on it further. Does that make sense? Do you have any other questions?
